title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (arXiv abstract page)
note: Single author (B. Neupane), stat.AP, v1 only, 2026-10-12. 24 configurations on ESHED-38 (38 homes, Erbil, daily, May 2020 to June 2025), 54,720 forecasts each from 48 weekly origins over a 359-day test, leads to 30 days. Best cut seasonal-naive scaled error by 20-25%; Chronos-2 zero-shot significantly best at 1 day, tied at 1 week. The page links no code or data repository.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (arXiv abstract page)
note: Abstract on weather: recorded weather improved no model. A quality screen found that on 68% of dates a temperature value repeats exactly on other dates, in three annual blocks covering almost the whole test period, so the author calls the value of weather information unresolved. Deep networks trained from scratch do not beat exponential smoothing on average; the survey adds negligible skill.

title: Same paper, full text (arXiv HTML), design
note: Test 2024-06-24 to 2025-06-17 (359 days), prior 180 days for tuning. 48 Sunday origins, leads 1-30 days, scored as h1, h7, h30; 48 x 30 x 38 forecasts. Metrics: MASE, relative geometric-mean MASE, sMAPE, MAE, RMSE, scaled CRPS, 80% coverage. Friedman, Nemenyi, Holm-Wilcoxon with houses as pairs. Foundation models: Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2 (univariate and weather tracks), TimesFM-2.5 (univariate).

title: Same paper, full text (arXiv HTML), results
note: Relative to seasonal naive: Chronos-2 at h1 gMASE 0.746, sCRPS 0.722, significantly ahead of all 23 others. At h7 gMASE 0.780 for Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5 and the univariate ensemble, statistically tied (adjusted p 0.51). At h30 the weather ensemble leads, gMASE 0.797, sCRPS 0.739, tied with the univariate ensemble, TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-2. No intervals on headline metrics.

title: Same paper, full text (arXiv HTML), weather track and limits
note: Weather track gives recorded weather for the forecast days (called an optimistic upper bound) to ARIMAX, LightGBM, XGBoost, N-HiTS, TFT, DeepAR, Chronos-2 and one ensemble; none improved. Limits listed: one city, one shared weather record that may be a reused annual sequence (unconfirmed with the data owners), one test year, 38 houses so many top differences are ties.

title: Same paper, full text (arXiv HTML), availability
note: Data: Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/dkts3x2yh5.2, CC BY 4.0. Code: a Kaggle notebook (one GPU, fixed seeds) available from the author on request, although the conclusion says the pipeline is released; no repository URL. No pre-registration is stated; ensemble members were fixed before testing. Chronos-2 is cited by its model card URL only, with no revision or package version.

title: Erbil Smart Home Energy Dataset - 38 houses [ESHED-38 (2020-2025)], Mendeley Data v2
note: Dataset by Truska Jaf and Ibrahim Ismael Hamarash, version 2, published 2026-05-20, CC BY 4.0. Daily kWh for 38 homes in Erbil from ministry smart meters, 14 May 2020 to 17 June 2025, with occupancy, building survey (December 2025) and weather from sensors near the houses. The page view showed only a download-all option, so the files were not inspected.
